defects.finding: These rest on a person's judgement, a signature or a record no catalogued system holds: SD-01.E, SD-02.E, SD-04.C, SD-04.E, SD-07.D, SD-09.B, SD-09.C, SD-10.C, SD-10.D, SD-11.D, SD-12.E, SD-16.C, SD-18.C, LM-03.D, LM-04.D, LM-05.D, LM-05.E, LM-06.C, LM-06.D, LM-07.D, LM-07.E, LM-07.F, LM-10.B, LM-10.C, LM-12.B, LM-12.D, LM-12.E, BC-02.C, BC-03.B, BC-04.B, BC-06.C, BC-08.D, BC-10.C. People only artifacts: escrow-verification-record, notices-to-customers-of-subprocessor-changes, secure-coding-training-completion-for-developers.
defects.proposal: No fix; checks can show the record exists and is on time, not that it is right. The control page should say so.

defects.finding: No template exists; the vulnerability-management-policy-with-timeframes and dependency triage artifacts point at a policy that is not a template.
defects.proposal: Create a template, or use the operations-security-policy section 'Finding and fixing vulnerabilities'.

defects.finding: No template exists for a backup policy.
defects.proposal: Create a template, or use operations-security-policy 'Backups and restore tests' with the continuity plan Appendix B.

defects.finding: No template exists for the published subprocessor list.
defects.proposal: Create one, held as a Documents entry linked to BC-06.

defects.finding: No postmortem template ships, so verity.incidents.postmortem_recorded cannot read the content (timeline, impact, root cause, detection gap).
defects.proposal: Add a postmortem template.

defects.finding: Tasks has no incident marker and no notice decision field, yet the security incident register (LM-07.D) is meant to live there.
defects.proposal: Ship a Security incident task template with a structured notice decision field, or the Phase 3.1 Incidents module, before verity.incidents.registered can run. Imported incidents need source and external_id for the connector reconciliation checks.

defects.finding: Task templates are not bound to controls (template_id exists, the binding does not), so verity.tasks.change_approved_independently cannot find its population.
defects.proposal: Add a binding between task templates and controls.

defects.item: tasks: recurring series to control link
defects.finding: Recurring task series are not linked to controls.
defects.proposal: Link the series to the control through the links table for verity.tasks.recurring_review_on_time.

defects.finding: verity.tasks.remediation_in_sla covers tasks, not issue actions until they are promoted to tasks.
defects.proposal: verity.tasks.capa_on_time reads issue actions directly.

defects.finding: Vulnerability settings hold remediation days per severity but no triage time, so SD-03.D and verity.vulns.triaged_in_time have no parameter to test against.
defects.proposal: Add a triage time per severity to the vulnerability settings.

defects.finding: A maximum risk acceptance length is not a setting.
defects.proposal: Add a maximum acceptance length setting (default 12 months) for verity.vulns.acceptances_approved.

defects.finding: Imported vulnerability scan reports record findings, not the targets scanned, so scan coverage (LM-11.B, now LM-13.B) cannot be shown from Verity: a clean asset leaves no trace.
defects.proposal: Add a target list to vuln_reports.

defects.finding: Vendors have no flag for customer data as opposed to staff data; Verity does not publish the subprocessor list or record customer notices. vendor_subprocessors is fourth parties, not the company's list.
defects.proposal: Add a customer data flag on vendors and a published list document linked to BC-06.

defects.finding: vendor_discovered_apps has no connector source until an identity provider connector ships, so BC-05 is manual in P1. A reason for ignored apps needs confirming in the schema.
defects.proposal: Feed discovered apps from the Phase 2 identity provider connectors; confirm an ignore reason field.

defects.finding: The security terms required per tier are not a tiering policy setting, and code ownership and escrow are not contract fields (needed for BC-10).
defects.proposal: Add required terms per tier to the tiering policy, and code ownership and escrow fields to contracts.

defects.finding: ISO certificates are documents without structured period fields, so their validity cannot be evaluated like a SOC report review.
defects.proposal: Add structured validity dates for certificates.

defects.finding: capabilities.json lists GitHub under CI and CD as planned for Phase 2 although the GitHub connector exists. Deployments, workflow runs and check results need new read permissions (unverified), so ci.* checks are P2 even on GitHub.
defects.proposal: Make the capability listing say GitHub version control is live and GitHub CI and CD reads are Phase 2.

defects.finding: Says 81 tests, and Appendix C of control-framework-requirements.md says Verity tests are planned; checks.json has 93 checks and the 30 verity checks run.
defects.proposal: Regenerate the catalogue and update Appendix C.

defects.finding: The LM-01 text says devices have no source in the catalogue because device management is not planned, while capabilities.json lists device_management (jamf, kandji, intune). Extractor's note, the document does not raise the conflict.
defects.proposal: Reconcile with mdm-and-endpoint-strategy.md and the devices research.

sources: NEED cloud_infrastructure: Configuration changes in production accounts in the period are listed with actor and time, and each is matched to an approved change or flagged.
NEED version_control: Merges to the infrastructure code repository in the period are listed with their reviews.
person (cloud change history export joined with change tickets)
artifacts_proposed.name: List of infrastructure, configuration, database and server software changes made in production in the period, with actor, time and the approved change each matches
artifacts_proposed.where: Cloud change history (for example the cloud audit trail) and merges to the infrastructure code repository, joined with change tickets.
artifacts_proposed.why: SD-01.B: ISO27001:A.8.19 and A.8.32 rely on SD-01 for software installed on servers and for infrastructure, configuration and database changes, but the population was merges only. Note: Server software installed by hand on a host is visible only to a host agent or the cloud's run command history.

sources: NEED ci_cd: Static analysis ran on every merged change and the merge waited for its result.

artifacts_proposed.name: List of all changes merged in the period with the static analysis run, its result and how each finding was handled
artifacts_proposed.where: Code scanning results in the version control system or the CI tool.
artifacts_proposed.why: SD-02.F: ISO27001:A.8.28 and A.8.29 rely on static analysis in the pipeline (rationales on SD-02 and SD-10). No objective tested that it ran.

artifacts_proposed.why: SD-15.B: New control. SD-15.C: New control.

sources: NEED observability: Each scheduled output job ran on time and passed its pre release checks.
person (delivery log with recipients and corrections)

artifacts_proposed.where: Job logs or the delivery system (exports, reports, files sent to customers).
artifacts_proposed.why: SD-16.B: New control. SD-16.C: New control. Note: Whether an output reached only the right recipient is shown by the delivery system's own records, read by people.

artifacts_proposed.where: Tasks module or tickets, one approved request per change, with the script attached.

sources: NEED cloud_infrastructure: Database audit logging is on for every production database.

artifacts_proposed.where: Database audit log or query log for production, reviewed by someone who did not run the changes.
artifacts_proposed.why: SD-17.C: New control. Note: Matching activity to approved changes is a person's review.

sources: NEED version_control: A component list with licences can be exported for each in scope repository from the provider's dependency graph.
NEED ci_cd: Each release build produced a component list stored with the release.
artifacts_proposed.name: Component list for each release, with component, version and licence
artifacts_proposed.where: Produced by the build or exported from the dependency graph of the version control system.
artifacts_proposed.why: SD-18.B: New objective on successor SD-18. SD-18.C: New objective on successor SD-18.

sources: NEED version_control: Dependency changes that add a component with a restricted licence are flagged at review.

artifacts_proposed.where: Tasks module, one approved task per exception, or the dependency review log.
artifacts_proposed.why: SD-18.C: New objective on successor SD-18. Note: Whether a licence fits how the product is sold is a legal judgement.

sources: NEED cloud_infrastructure: The central log store has a retention lock or object lock, and system administrators cannot delete it.
NEED observability: Roles that can delete logs or change retention in the observability tool are listed.
artifacts_proposed.name: Retention, immutability and delete permission settings of the central log store
artifacts_proposed.where: Settings of the log store in the cloud console or observability tool, with the list of roles that can delete logs or change retention.
artifacts_proposed.why: LM-02.C: Retention and protection against administrators were one objective. ISO27001:A.8.15 claims both; protection moves to LM-02.G, and retention gains a settings test instead of an interview alone. LM-02.G: Split out of LM-02.C; ISO27001:A.8.15 (full) and A.5.28 rely on protected logs.

sources: NEED observability: A monitor alerts when any listed log source sends nothing for longer than the set gap, and each alert was followed up.
module tasks: Issues raised for log gaps, check verity.tasks.remediation_in_sla
artifacts_proposed.name: Alerts raised when a log source stopped sending, with follow up
artifacts_proposed.where: The observability tool's monitor history, with a ticket or issue for each gap.
artifacts_proposed.why: LM-02.F: Split out of LM-02.B; ISO27001:A.8.15 and SOC2:CC2.1 rely on complete logs.

sources: module documents: Acknowledgement campaign on the incident response plan targeted at the incident roles, check verity.policies.acknowledged
artifacts_proposed.name: Acknowledgement of the current incident response plan by everyone who holds a role in it
artifacts_proposed.where: Documents module, an acknowledgement campaign on the plan targeted at the incident roles.
artifacts_proposed.why: LM-07.C: Sharing the plan and reviewing it were one objective with different evidence and cadence. Review moves to LM-07.G.

sources: module tasks: Attachments on incident issues with uploader and time

artifacts_proposed.why: LM-07.F: ISO27001:A.5.28 is mapped to LM-07 on the evidence procedure, but only the written procedure was examined. Note: Whether evidence was captured without changing it is a person's account.

sources: NEED cloud_infrastructure: Each backup store has a copy in another region or account and an immutability or lock setting.

artifacts_proposed.where: Backup vault or snapshot settings from the cloud console.
artifacts_proposed.why: BC-01.D: Storage protection and restore rights were one objective. Restore rights move to BC-01.E, and storage protection gains a settings test.

control_changes.reason: SOC2:CC8.1 (full) and ISO27001:A.8.19, A.8.32 rely on SD-01 for every kind of production change, including server software, infrastructure, configuration and database changes. SD-01.B tested a population of merges only, so it is reworded to cover the whole change population.

objective_changes.statement: Every production change released in the period appeared on the change list: application releases checked against the deployments, and infrastructure, configuration, database and server software changes checked against the cloud change history and administrator activity.
objective_changes.why: ISO27001:A.8.19 and A.8.32 rely on SD-01 for software installed on servers and for infrastructure, configuration and database changes, but the population was merges only.

control_changes.reason: ISO27001:A.8.28 and A.8.29 rely on static analysis in the pipeline, which no objective tested. SD-02.F is added. SD-02.E applies only when Processing Integrity (SOC2:PI1.3) is in scope and reads not applicable otherwise.

objective_changes.statement: The security tests the engineering standard names, such as static analysis, ran on every change merged in the period, and each finding they raised was fixed, dismissed with a reason or carried as an approved exception before release.
objective_changes.why: ISO27001:A.8.28 and A.8.29 rely on static analysis in the pipeline (rationales on SD-02 and SD-10). No objective tested that it ran.

control_changes.reason: SD-03 bundles vulnerability scanning (SOC2:CC6.8, CC7.1, ISO27001:A.8.8, A.8.28, A.8.29) with a component list and licence review (ISO27001:A.5.32). The licence review has a different owner (legal with engineering), a different remediation (replace the component or approve the licence) and different applicability (a SOC 2 only workspace can leave it out), and no operating objective tested it.

successors.name: Software component list and licence review

requirements.rationale: Moved from SD-03. The component list records each open source component's licence, and licences that conflict with how the product is used or sold are reviewed before release. Commercial licences sit with GOV-05 and rights in staff work with HR-02.

A component list per release shows which third party software each release contains, which is the software part of supply chain visibility. Vulnerability scanning of those components stays with SD-03.

objective_changes.statement: The dependency triage standard is approved. It names the scanner for code dependencies and container images, sets triage and fix timeframes by severity, says which new critical findings fail a build and how exceptions are approved.
objective_changes.why: The component list with licences moves to the proposed SD-18.A.

objective_changes.statement: The component and licence standard is approved. It says which builds produce a component list, which licences are allowed, restricted or not allowed for how the product is used or sold, and who may approve an exception.
objective_changes.why: New objective on successor SD-18.

objective_changes.statement: Each release in the period had a component list, produced by the build, naming each component, its version and its licence.
objective_changes.why: New objective on successor SD-18.

objective_changes.statement: Components with a restricted or not allowed licence were found before release and removed, replaced or approved as an exception with a reason.
objective_changes.why: New objective on successor SD-18.

mapping_changes.rationale: Moves to SD-18 with the component list and licence review.

It moves to the proposed SD-15. What stays answers SOC2:PI1.2 and ISO27001:A.8.26, A.8.28, so SD-05 must be adoptable without Processing Integrity (onboarding lists it as on demand for PI only).

objective_changes.why: Moves to SD-15 with the activity it tests.

control_changes.reason: ISO27001:A.8.25 and A.8.27 (both full) and A.8.26, A.8.29 rest on SD-10. Objective B bundled approval of security requirements before build and the check before release that A.8.29 relies on. B is reworded and F added. A split into a separate design review control was weighed and not proposed: one owner, one population, and the objectives already separate the evidence.

objective_changes.statement: Each new application, major feature and acquired system in the period had its security requirements recorded and approved at design review before it was built or bought.
objective_changes.why: The original bundled approval before build and verification before release, two moments with different evidence. Verification moves to SD-10.F.

objective_changes.statement: Before release, each of those systems was checked against its approved security requirements, and any requirement not met was fixed or accepted by the approver.
objective_changes.why: ISO27001:A.8.29 relies on SD-10 for acceptance against security requirements before release.

control_changes.name: Processing error handling and correction
control_changes.reason: SOC2:PI1.2 and PI1.3 rest on SD-05 and SD-08 alone, each partial (LD-14). Error handling and correction is the missing activity (onboarding section 7). Receives SD-05.D.

requirements.rationale: Rejected and duplicate inputs are held in a monitored queue and corrected, so input errors are not lost. Validation at the boundary comes from SD-05.
Processing errors are logged, corrected with approval and reprocessed against the reconciliation. Detecting the error comes from SD-08.

objective_changes.statement: The error handling procedure is approved. It says where rejected inputs and processing errors are held, who reviews them, how a correction is approved and reprocessed, and the time allowed for each.
objective_changes.why: New control.

objective_changes.statement: Each processing error in the period was logged with the date, the records affected, the cause and the correction, and was closed within the time the procedure allows.
objective_changes.why: New control.

objective_changes.statement: Corrections and reprocessing were approved by someone other than the person who made them, and the reprocessed run reconciled before its output was released.
objective_changes.why: New control.
Moved from SD-05.D with the activity it tests.

control_changes.name: Output delivery and review
control_changes.reason: SOC2:PI1.4 rests on SD-08 alone, and the SD-08 rationale says delivery to the right recipient needs its own check (onboarding section 7).

requirements.rationale: Outputs are checked before release and reach only their intended recipients on time, with wrong or late outputs corrected. SD-08 shows the outputs were produced.

objective_changes.statement: Each key output has an approved specification of its recipients, format and timing, the checks made before release, and how a wrong or late output is withdrawn and corrected.
objective_changes.why: New control.

objective_changes.statement: Each scheduled output in the period was produced on time and passed its completeness and accuracy checks before release.
objective_changes.why: New control.

objective_changes.statement: Outputs reached only their intended recipients, and each misdirected, late or wrong output was recorded, corrected and, where a customer was affected, reported to them.
objective_changes.why: New control.

control_changes.tenant_impact: adoption proposal: offer when Processing Integrity is elected

control_changes.reason: SOC2:CC8.1 names changes to data. Direct changes to production data outside the application are tested by every SOC 1 and SOC 2 auditor and no SD control covers them (onboarding section 9).

requirements.rationale: Changes made straight to production data, outside the application and its release path, are requested, approved by someone other than the person who runs them, logged and reconciled with the database activity. The other change controls cover code and infrastructure.
Brings data fixes run by hand inside change control: approval before the change, a limited group who may run it, and a check of the database activity against approved changes.

objective_changes.statement: The procedure for changing production data outside the application is approved. It says when a direct change is allowed, who may request, approve and run one, that it runs as a reviewed script where possible, and what is logged.
objective_changes.why: New control.

objective_changes.statement: Every direct change to production data in the period was requested and approved before it ran, by someone other than the person who ran it.
objective_changes.why: New control.

objective_changes.statement: Only the listed people could change production data directly, and the database activity for the period matched the approved changes.
objective_changes.why: New control.

control_changes.reason: ISO27001:A.8.15 (full) needs collection, retention, protection, gap detection and review. LM-02.B and LM-02.C each bundled two of these with different evidence. Reworded B and C, added F (gap alerts) and G (protection from administrators).

objective_changes.statement: Sign in, access change, administrator and application audit events from every in scope system reached the central log store.
objective_changes.why: Gap alerting moves to its own objective, LM-02.F, because it is shown by different evidence (monitor and alert history, not source coverage).

objective_changes.statement: Logs were kept for at least 12 months with the latest 3 months searchable at once.
objective_changes.why: Retention and protection against administrators were one objective. ISO27001:A.8.15 claims both; protection moves to LM-02.G, and retention gains a settings test instead of an interview alone.

objective_changes.statement: A source that stopped sending logs raised an alert, and each such alert was followed up until the source was sending again.
objective_changes.why: Split out of LM-02.B; ISO27001:A.8.15 and SOC2:CC2.1 rely on complete logs.

objective_changes.statement: The administrators of a system could not change or delete its logs, and the few people who can change retention or delete logs in the central store were named and approved.
objective_changes.why: Split out of LM-02.C; ISO27001:A.8.15 (full) and A.5.28 rely on protected logs.

control_changes.reason: ISO27001:10.2 asks that corrective action is checked for effect. LM-05.E added. A.5.27 (full) is otherwise covered.

objective_changes.statement: Each closed corrective action was checked for effect, by confirming the cause did not recur or by a verification recorded by someone other than its owner.
objective_changes.why: ISO27001:10.2 asks that the effect of corrective action is reviewed; LM-05 maps to it and no objective tested it.

control_changes.reason: ISO27001:A.5.28 is mapped on the evidence procedure, but only the written plan was examined; LM-07.F tests that evidence was handled as the plan sets. LM-07.C bundled sharing the plan and reviewing it; C is reworded and G added.

objective_changes.statement: The current plan was given to everyone who holds a role in it, and each of them acknowledged the current version.
objective_changes.why: Sharing the plan and reviewing it were one objective with different evidence and cadence. Review moves to LM-07.G.

objective_changes.statement: Where an incident needed evidence, it was collected and kept as the plan sets, with a record of who collected and handled each item and when.
objective_changes.why: ISO27001:A.5.28 is mapped to LM-07 on the evidence procedure, but only the written procedure was examined.

objective_changes.statement: The plan was reviewed in the last 12 months and after each significant incident, and each review was recorded.
objective_changes.why: Split out of LM-07.C (shared and reviewed).

control_changes.reason: One activity, on call cover with escalation, for SOC2:CC7.2 and CC7.4. It has no ISO mapping, so an ISO only workspace would not see it; ISO27001:A.5.24 partial is proposed.

mapping_changes.rationale: An on call rotation with escalation makes the response roles the plan names reachable at any hour. The plan itself comes from LM-07 and the exercise from LM-10.

control_changes.reason: SOC2:CC7.1 and ISO27001:A.8.8 are both full on LM-11, which bundles discovery coverage (scanners, targets reconciled with the asset inventory, authenticated scans) with triage, remediation and risk acceptance. They have different owners (whoever runs the scanners versus each asset owner), cadences (scan interval versus per finding SLA) and failure conclusions (a coverage gap is not a late fix). Continuous compliance plan section 4 names this split. Scanner checks then map to LM-13, register checks to LM-11.

requirements.rationale: Scans of infrastructure, containers, dependencies and the external surface at the set frequency, with targets reconciled to the asset inventory, are the discovery half of vulnerability detection. Handling what is found stays with LM-11.
Finding technical weaknesses across the whole estate, with authenticated scans and coverage gaps followed up. Evaluating and fixing them stays with LM-11.

objective_changes.why: Moves to LM-13 with the activity it tests.

objective_changes.statement: The vulnerability management policy sets the scan scope for infrastructure, containers, dependencies and the external surface, the minimum scan frequency, when authenticated scans are required and what counts as a significant change that triggers an extra scan.
objective_changes.why: New objective on successor LM-13.

objective_changes.statement: Failed, partial and unauthenticated scans, and targets the scanner could not reach, were found and followed up, so a gap in coverage was not read as a clean result.
objective_changes.why: New objective on successor LM-13.

mapping_changes.rationale: LM-11 keeps the register, triage, remediation times and risk acceptance. Discovery coverage moves to LM-13, so LM-11 alone no longer covers the whole criterion.
Same split: evaluating and treating weaknesses stays, finding them across the estate moves to LM-13.

objective_changes.statement: Backups were encrypted at rest, and at least one copy sat in a separate region, account or site on immutable or offline storage.
objective_changes.why: Storage protection and restore rights were one objective. Restore rights move to BC-01.E, and storage protection gains a settings test.

objective_changes.statement: Rights to restore or delete backups were held by a small group that was reviewed in the period.
objective_changes.why: Split out of BC-01.D.

objective_changes.statement: The configuration, infrastructure code and images needed to rebuild each service were kept in versioned storage covered by the backup policy.
objective_changes.why: ISO27001:A.8.13 covers copies of software and systems as well as data. BC-01.A names them; nothing tested them.

control_changes.reason: ISO27001:A.8.14 (full) is a separate Annex A control, chosen on its own in the Statement of Applicability, about technical redundancy. BC-03 bundled it with continuity planning (SOC2:CC9.1, ISO27001:A.5.29, A.5.30). The two have different owners (the business continuity owner versus engineering), different evidence (a plan and an exercise versus cloud configuration and a failover test) and different remediation (rewrite and exercise the plan versus change the architecture). A cloud check on zones and standbys needs a control to map to that is not the plan.

successors.name: Redundancy and failover of critical services

requirements.rationale: Moved from BC-03. The redundancy each critical service relies on is recorded against its recovery targets, kept in place and failed over in a yearly test, which shows it is enough for the availability promised.
Redundant components and a tested failover are part of the recovery infrastructure. Backups come from BC-01 and environmental protection from PE-01 and PE-03.
A tested failover shows technology can meet the recovery targets the continuity plan sets. Data restores come from BC-02.

objective_changes.statement: The continuity and recovery plan is approved. It sets recovery time and data loss targets for each critical service, activation criteria, roles, and how customers and staff are told.
objective_changes.why: The redundancy each service relies on moves to the proposed BC-09.A.

objective_changes.statement: The plan was exercised in the last 12 months against a realistic scenario, recording who took part and the results compared with each recovery target.
objective_changes.why: Failover of the redundant parts moves to the proposed BC-09.C.
Moves to BC-09 with the activity it tests.

objective_changes.statement: For each critical service the redundancy it relies on to meet its recovery targets is recorded, such as several availability zones, a standby database or a secondary region, and approved by the engineering lead.
objective_changes.why: New objective on successor BC-09.

objective_changes.statement: The recorded redundancy was in place throughout the period for each critical service.
objective_changes.why: New objective on successor BC-09.

objective_changes.statement: Failover of the redundant parts was tested in the last 12 months, and the time to fail over was compared with the recovery targets.
objective_changes.why: New objective on successor BC-09.

mapping_changes.rationale: Moves to BC-09 with the redundancy record and the failover test.

control_changes.reason: ISO27001:A.5.22 relies on suppliers no longer used being removed with access revoked. BC-07.D bundled the yearly review with offboarding, an event per vendor with its own record; D reworded and E added.

objective_changes.statement: The register was reviewed in the last 12 months, with contract dates and renewal points checked for each vendor.
objective_changes.why: Offboarding with access revoked moves to BC-07.E: it is an event per vendor, not part of the yearly review.

objective_changes.statement: Vendors no longer used were offboarded: their access was revoked, their copy of company data returned or deleted, and the offboarding recorded.
objective_changes.why: Split out of BC-07.D; ISO27001:A.5.22 rationale relies on removal with access revoked.

control_changes.reason: BC-08 maps to ten requirements. ISO27001:A.8.30 (outsourced development) applies only where a supplier builds software for the company and needs its own evidence (code ownership, acceptance testing of deliveries, escrow); bundled in BC-08 it cannot be marked not applicable on its own in the Statement of Applicability. It moves to BC-10. BC-08 objectives are also revised: B repeated BC-07.C and becomes tiering, E bundled contract terms (A.5.20) with findings (now F), and G is added for ongoing delivery review (A.5.22, A.8.21).

requirements.rationale: Contracts with suppliers that build software set security requirements, code ownership, audit rights and escrow where needed, and each delivery is reviewed and tested before it goes live. Choosing the supplier stays with BC-08 and code review with SD-06.
Manages the risk of a business partner that writes software the company runs. General vendor due diligence comes from BC-08.

objective_changes.statement: Each supplier with access to systems or data had a current tier from a tiering assessment, and that tier set the depth of its assessment.
objective_changes.why: As written it repeated BC-07.C (register complete). BC-08 relies on BC-07 for the population and tests its own step, tiering.

objective_changes.statement: Contracts carried the security terms the procedure sets for the vendor's tier, such as incident notice, audit rights, limits on subcontracting and data return at exit.
objective_changes.why: Contract terms (ISO27001:A.5.20) and tracking of findings were one objective. Findings move to BC-08.F.

objective_changes.statement: Findings and accepted risks from assessments were tracked to closure, or to an acceptance with an owner and an expiry.
objective_changes.why: Split out of BC-08.E.

objective_changes.statement: At each reassessment of a critical vendor, its delivery against the agreed security and service levels was reviewed, and a material change, such as a breach, new ownership or a new subservice provider, led to an early review.
objective_changes.why: ISO27001:A.5.22 and A.8.21 rationales rely on checking delivered service levels; no objective tested it.

objective_changes.statement: Contracts with suppliers that build software for the company set the security requirements, who owns the code, audit rights and, where a critical system depends on the supplier's code, an escrow arrangement.
objective_changes.why: New objective on successor BC-10.

objective_changes.statement: Each delivery from a development supplier was reviewed by a member of staff and tested against its security requirements before it went live.
objective_changes.why: New objective on successor BC-10.

objective_changes.statement: Where escrow is required, the deposit was checked as complete and current at each review.
objective_changes.why: New objective on successor BC-10.
